purpose: Tests the noncommutativity criterion: does order of E-null suffixes matter? Both logit-bias and K_a models predict order-independence (additive/commutative). If TV(response(AB), response(BA)) > eps_eq, the monoid is genuinely non-commutative and neither scalar model can explain the data. This is the single strongest discriminator for native non-scalar structure.

predictions.H_commutative: Order does not matter: TV(AB, BA) < eps_eq for all contexts. Consistent with logit-bias, K_a, and scalar character models.
predictions.H_noncommutative: Order matters: TV(AB, BA) > eps_eq for some contexts. Defeats logit-bias, K_a, AND scalar character simultaneously. Establishes genuine non-scalar monoid structure.
predictions.decisive_test: TV distance between A_then_B and B_then_A response distributions per context. eps_eq = 0.01. If max TV > 0.01 across contexts, declare noncommutative.

estimated_calls: 3 vars x 8 vals x 1 depth x 5 conditions = 120 calls, ~2.5 min CPU
